personalitySettings.title: Assistant tone & response style
personalitySettings.deepResearchNote: Breaks your question into sub-questions, researches each separately, then synthesizes one answer. Several sequential model calls on the same model — noticeably slower than a normal reply, not multiple AI models running at once. Independent from the response style above: it changes how much research goes into an answer, not its tone — the two combine (e.g. Deep Research + Succinct still synthesizes a short final answer).
personalitySettings.adaptiveRoutingNote: Classifies each message and picks which downloaded model answers it (e.g. a lightweight model for small talk, a stronger one for research/comparison questions), switching between them as needed. On by default and independent from Deep Research — if it fails for any reason, chat falls back to your normal active model automatically, it never leaves you without a response.

aboutScreen.title: About NIDO
aboutScreen.licensesBody: The license of NIDO, of each AI model, of the Wikipedia text it carries and of the libraries it is built with.
aboutScreen.noticesBody: On a PC, NIDO tells you at the scheduled time while it is open; if it stays resident in the tray, also with the window closed. A computer that is off or asleep cannot notify you: when it comes back, NIDO shows you what came due in the meantime, saying it is late. With the vault locked, the system notice stays generic and the text waits for you at unlock.
aboutScreen.developmentBody: NIDO is a free, independent project. Its development and maintenance are sustained without advertising, accounts, or paid features. For those who have asked how to contribute, the project provides these addresses for voluntary contributions in USDC or other compatible tokens. A contribution provides no advantages, unlocks no features, and creates no account. Contributions are made from each person's own wallet; NIDO does not process payments or verify transactions inside the app. Send only through the indicated network: a transfer sent through the wrong network may be permanently lost.
aboutScreen.developmentSolanaLabel: USDC or another compatible token · Solana
aboutScreen.developmentBaseLabel: USDC or another compatible token · Base
aboutScreen.mobileBody: NIDO also lives on Android, with the same idea as always: everything happens on your device, with no accounts and nothing of yours sent to any server. The phone app is free and open source, and it installs from its releases page, outside the stores, like this one.
aboutScreen.reportBody: If something goes wrong, the app prepares a short summary and shows it to you in full before you do anything with it. It only carries data about the app and your computer: the version, the system, the model in use and the last recorded error, if there is one. It never carries your messages, your notes, your memory or your contacts. The app sends nothing: you copy the report and paste it into the repository form, or open the report page in your browser when you are online. We read every report, and everything that can be fixed is fixed in a later version.

guide.title: Learn to use NIDO
guide.subtitle: Short lessons to get the most out of your NIDO on this computer. Everything works with no internet.
guide.try: Tap an example and it is typed into the chat, ready to send. Nothing is ever sent on its own.
guide.toolOff: One of this lesson's features is off in the agent permissions. To turn it on, go to Settings and open the agent permissions.

lessons.title: Talking to NIDO
lessons.what: Talk to it like you would to anyone. Greetings and short chat are answered right away, without waiting for any model. For everything else, NIDO works out the answer with its AI model, which lives on your computer, and checks what it claims against the sources it has at hand before serving it to you. Under each model answer, a badge says how it was checked: "full check" or "word check".
lessons.tip: The model's first answer can take a few seconds while it gets ready. On a computer, NIDO can load larger models than on a tablet, so that short wait buys you better answers.

lessons.title: Choosing a model
lessons.what: The model is the brain that lives on your computer: the larger it is, the better its answers, but the more memory it needs and the longer it takes to get ready the first time. In the Models section you see the ones available for this computer, each with its size and the memory it needs, and the app points out the one recommended for your machine. Large models, like the 7B or the LFM2.5-8B, are normal on a computer: they download once and stay here, with no accounts and no internet.
steps: Open the Models section in the sidebar.
Look at each model's size and memory count, and at which one is recommended for this computer.
Download the one you choose and load it: the chat uses it from that moment.
lessons.tip: If a large model takes a while to load the first time, that is normal: it gets ready once, and after that answers arrive faster.

lessons.title: Time, calculations and conversions
lessons.what: Some questions need no thinking: the time, an arithmetic problem, or turning one unit into another. The app itself answers those, right away and with the exact figure, without loading any model. Conversions cover physical units: distance, weight, temperature, volume and time.
examples: how much is 10 miles in kilometers?
lessons.tip: Money is not converted: without internet there are no exchange rates, and if you ask to change one currency into another, NIDO tells you exactly that instead of making a rate up.

lessons.title: Reminders, notes and memory through the chat
lessons.what: Ask NIDO to keep things for you: a reminder, a note, a fact you want it to remember. Everything is stored in your computer's encrypted memory, and you get it back by asking in your own words. A reminder can be saved with its repetition: every day, every week, every month or every year. Everything you save can be seen and deleted whenever you want in the Memory section, in its “My memory” list.
steps: Open the Memory section in the sidebar.
In the “My memory” list, look through the four tabs: Facts, Notes, People and Reminders.
To delete a row, tap its delete button and confirm on the same button: the list updates right away.
examples: remind me to drink water in 1 hour
save a note: the workshop closes on Mondays
remember that the library opens at 9
what notes do I have saved?
lessons.tip: Reminders stay saved and you can check them whenever you like. Your agenda already lives in the Agenda section, and NIDO tells you when you open the app once the time of a notice has come.

lessons.title: Calendar and contacts
lessons.what: NIDO keeps your events and your people in the Agenda on this PC: events with their time and their reminder, and contacts with their phone, their email and their birthday. What you save in chat and what you see in the Agenda section is the same thing.
steps: Ask for an event in chat, with the day and the time: NIDO saves it to your calendar.
Open the Agenda section: under Calendar you see the month and your events, and you can create or fix one by hand.
Under Contacts you save your people with their birthday: NIDO prepares the reminder every year.
When you look someone up in chat, NIDO answers from these contacts. On this PC it cannot call or text: it shows you the saved number so you can dial from your phone.
lessons.tip: An event with a reminder stays armed in your Agenda: NIDO tells you when you open the app once its time has come.

lessons.title: Scheduled tasks
lessons.what: A task is an instruction NIDO carries out on its own at a set time, like summarizing your notes every morning. Tasks run while NIDO is open and the vault is unlocked, with the safe tools: a task can read your notes, your calendar and your inbox, and save notes. It can never send messages, call, pair or open other apps.
steps: Open Settings and go to the Notices zone: the scheduled tasks card lives there.
Create the task with its name, what it should do, the time and the days of the week.
At its time, the task runs on its own and its result stays on the card, with the last run and whether it went well.
If NIDO was closed at its time, the task runs when you open it; if NIDO stays resident in the tray, it lets you know at the scheduled time.
lessons.tip: Pausing a task does not delete it: switch it off and switch it back on whenever you like. Its history stays on the card.

lessons.title: Speaking and listening
lessons.what: NIDO can listen to you and read aloud, all on this PC and offline. Dictation turns your voice into text inside the writing box: you see it before sending and it is never sent on its own. Reading speaks the answers with NIDO's voice; in Emergency, the speaker button reads the CPR guide step by step.
steps: If it is your first time, open Settings, Voice section, and download the voice models: the listening one is 487 MB and the speech one 350 MB, just once.
To dictate, tap Dictate by voice, the microphone next to the writing box, and speak in phrases: each phrase appears as text and you can keep speaking or fix it before sending.
To hear an answer, tap Read aloud, the speaker under the answer; tap again to stop the reading right away.
In Settings, Voice section, you can turn on automatic reading of every answer and turn dictation off if you do not use it.
lessons.tip: If NIDO's voice is not downloaded, reading can use your operating system's voice when the fallback is on: it sounds different, and the Voice section always tells you which one is speaking.

lessons.title: Emergencies
lessons.what: The Emergency section holds the topics of the fixed table, in their order: first if you are thinking of harming yourself and suspected carbon monoxide; then resuscitation, choking, heavy bleeding and burns; and last the emergency number. Tap a topic or say it in your own words and I will answer in the chat. The fixed emergency answers always arrive, even without a model; the other guides come from your verified sources and the loaded model. If there is immediate danger, call the emergency number first from your phone: the computer shows you the number, but it does not dial for you.
steps: Open the Emergency section in the sidebar.
Tap the topic that fits, or say it in your own words in the section's field: the answer arrives in the chat.
If you tap the emergency number, the answer shows it to you checked and with its source.
Call from your phone: NIDO on the computer does not dial; it shows you the number so you can call it yourself.
lessons.tip: If one day you type an emergency into the chat, NIDO does not improvise: it answers with a fixed safe text, written so you can act in order, and it never makes health advice up.

lessons.title: The encrypted memory and its gate
lessons.what: Everything NIDO keeps for you (your conversations, your notes, your reminders and your settings) is stored encrypted on your computer, inside a vault that only opens with your password. Without that password, the app hands over nothing: not your things, not even a hint of what is inside.
steps: Close the app and open it again.
The gate asks for your password before showing anything.
Type it and come in: your conversations and your things are intact, just as you left them.
lessons.tip: If you forget the password, there is no way to recover what is stored: the gate keeps no copy of your key, and what is stored is lost with it. Keep your password somewhere safe, off the computer if you can.

lessons.title: Asking without internet
lessons.what: The packs you have installed live on your computer, and NIDO answers from there, with no internet. The Essentials pack holds guides on first aid, health, disasters and survival in Spanish, English and Portuguese, and the Local pack holds the checked emergency numbers for each country. When an answer comes from a guide, the evidence card shows you which one and from what source.
examples: how do you do CPR on an adult?
lessons.tip: If you ask something no installed guide covers, NIDO says so instead of making up an answer with a fake source: it offers to open the full guide when there is one, and when there is not, it stays with not knowing.

lessons.title: Searching in Spanish and Portuguese
lessons.what: You can ask in your own language even when the guide that answers is written in another one. With multilingual search, NIDO compares the meaning of your question with the meaning of the guides it has installed, not just the words, and so it finds the right guide even if it is in English. The evidence card shows you which guide it used and where it comes from, so you can check it yourself.
examples: how do you treat a mild burn?
lessons.tip: Ask the way you would say it, without translating anything in your head: the search does the crossing, and the answer reaches you in your language with its source in view.

lessons.title: Packs and the SALVORA note
lessons.what: A pack is a book of knowledge that NIDO keeps on your computer: a file with guides, signed by whoever publishes it, NIDO or SALVORA PACKS. The packs section, inside "Knowledge base and documents" in Settings, is where they are managed: the list shows the official catalog packs and the ones you add from a file, each with its origin, its edition and its state. In the Library they are read: an installed pack appears with its guides, ready to read with no model and no internet. At the foot of the section lives the SALVORA note, the same one as in the About screen, served from the same source.
steps: Open Settings and go into "Knowledge base and documents".

Look down the list: each pack says who publishes it (NIDO or SALVORA PACKS), its edition and its state: up to date, with an earlier version in use that keeps serving, or not installed. If a pack was made for the other search model, its row carries a notice: with that pack, search works by words.
Install the one you are missing from its row: the app downloads it and checks its fingerprint before counting it as installed.

To add a pack you have as a file, use "Add a pack from a file" and choose the file: before copying anything, the confirmation names who signed it. If the file is not signed by NIDO or by SALVORA PACKS, or it changed since it was signed, the app rejects it and tells you why, copying nothing.
Open the Library and go into the pack: its guides are there to read in full, with no model and no internet.

Read the SALVORA note at the foot of the section: buying SALVORA guide packs at salvorapacks.com helps NIDO keep being developed, and buying unlocks nothing, because NIDO has no locked content. The packs you buy come in through this same signed door, like any other.
If you want to remove a pack you added from a file, its row has the remove action. Catalog packs are not removed from this section.
lessons.tip: A pack's signature proves who published it and that the file has not changed since it was signed; it does not prove its content is good. That is why the origin is visible on every row: before installing or adding a pack, look at who signs it and decide with that in view.

lessons.title: Your documents: ask about them
lessons.what: Besides the packs, NIDO can read your own documents: a contract, the boiler manual, the notes from a meeting. You add them from the "Your documents" card in "Knowledge base and documents", in Settings, and they stay in your encrypted base, on this computer and nowhere else. From then on they are one more source: when you ask in the chat, the answer can come from your document, and then the citation gives its name and the exact page. If the page was a photo or a scan, its text is read with optical recognition (OCR) inside the app, and the passage says so: it carries its provenance mark.
steps: Open Settings and go to "Knowledge base and documents".
On the "Your documents" card, press "Add documents" and choose one or more files: text files, PDFs or images.
Wait for the confirmation naming what was imported. If some file could not be read in full, the notice says so; what did come in can already be asked about.
Go to the chat and ask about its content, the way you would ask someone who has read it: "what pressure does the boiler take, according to the manual?".
Look at the citation under the answer: it gives the document and the page ("Rental contract · p. 7"). The app fills that page in from the stored document; the model does not write it.

Tap the source to open it: the panel shows the whole page with its header ("p. 7 of 128") and that page's text, served from your encrypted base. The original file is not opened, and it does not need to still be where it was.
In the Library you can see how much each collection takes, with its real size. From there you can turn it off so it stops answering without deleting it, export it to Downloads, or delete it for good.
lessons.tip: When an answer cites your document, the page rules: open it and check the passage before trusting it. And the other way round: if the model mentions a page in its prose and there is no citation under it, that is just its wording, not a source.

lessons.title: Deep research
lessons.what: Some questions deserve more than one quick answer. Deep research is a mode you turn on for a question: NIDO splits it into smaller questions, looks each one up in your packs and your documents, checks every part against its sources, and writes one report. One model does the work, in passes, so it takes longer than a normal answer. Everything happens on your computer.
steps: Turn it on with the Deep research chip next to the message box; it also lives in Settings. It applies to the questions you send while it is on.
Before anything runs, you see the Research plan: the smaller questions your question was split into, and what the run is expected to cost. Nothing is spent until you press Research now.

The plan is yours to touch: remove a question, add one of your own, and choose where it looks, your packs, your documents, or both, with the source count of each. What you add goes through the same safety check as everything else.

Each pass comes back judged: supported, partial (with the unsupported sentences removed and counted), or with no sources at all. If nothing turns up anywhere, NIDO says your local library has nothing on it instead of inventing a report.

Read the same report four ways, Full report, Executive brief, Side by side and Timeline, from the style selector under the answer. Changing the style changes the shape, never what was claimed or its citations. Under Every claim, with its source, tap a claim to open the passage it came from, and the run receipt shows the model, the time and the tokens.

If you stop a run, the work is not lost: each finished part is saved in your encrypted memory, and tomorrow you can resume the session where it closed from the saved sessions list. Deleting a session deletes that document of yours, and the app asks you to confirm it first.
An emergency is never researched: if your question uncovers one, the protected guide answers instead, even with the mode on.
examples: How did Roman aqueducts carry water across valleys?
lessons.tip: The report is saved in your encrypted memory together with its receipts. Export it with the button under the answer when you want a copy in your Downloads; nothing leaves the computer on its own.

lessons.title: The About screen and donations
lessons.what: The "About and licenses" tab in Settings says who makes NIDO and how it is sustained. It holds the app's identity with the version you have installed, the open source card (NIDO is free software, under the MIT License, and its code lives in its public repository), the licenses entry, the voluntary SALVORA support note, the "NIDO development" card with the donation addresses the app only shows and copies, and the block for reporting a problem if something goes wrong. Nothing on this screen sells anything or asks for an account.
steps: Open Settings and go into "About and licenses".
Look at the version badge: it shows the installed version, read from the app itself.
Read the whole SALVORA note: buying SALVORA guide packs at salvorapacks.com helps NIDO keep being developed, and buying unlocks nothing, because NIDO has no locked content.

If you want to contribute, on the "NIDO development" card copy the address for the network you use, Solana or Base, with the "Copy" button or by tapping the address itself, and check the "Address copied" notice: what was copied is the address shown, character by character.

If something goes wrong, use "Report a problem": the app puts together a short summary and shows it to you in full; you copy it with "Copy report" and paste it into the repository form. The app sends nothing over the network: the person sends, the app only prepares.
lessons.tip: Contributing is voluntary and brings no advantages: it unlocks no features and creates no account. Send only through the network named next to each address, because a transfer sent through the wrong network may be lost for good. NIDO never asks for contributions in the chat: support lives only on this screen.

lessons.title: Tone, and if something goes wrong
lessons.what: NIDO can answer you in different ways: shorter, in more depth, as a summary, or however you ask with your own instructions. That is the tone, and it lives in Settings: it is kept on your computer and governs the answers the model writes. And if one day the app closes by itself or something fails, there is a place to see the reason and prepare the report, without the app sending anything over the network.
steps: Open Settings and go into "Assistant tone & response style".
Pick a style: "Succinct & Direct", which is the one selected by default, "Thorough & Detailed", "Executive Summary" or "Custom".

If you pick "Custom", write your instructions in the field that appears, for example how you want things explained to you. They are kept as a private encrypted setting, capped at 2,000 characters, and they never leave your computer.

Go back to the chat and type the example below: the answer arrives already in the chosen tone. Next to the writing field there is also a chip showing the chosen tone: tap it to go to the tone section in Settings and change it there. If you change the tone while an answer is on its way, the change applies from the next turn: what is already being written does not change.

If something goes wrong, open Settings and go into "About and licenses": under "Report a problem" the app puts together a short summary, with the last recorded error if there is one, and shows it to you in full before you do anything with it. With "Copy report" you copy it and paste it into the repository form. The app sends nothing: sending it is your own gesture.
lessons.tip: The tone governs only the answers the model writes. Greetings and the app's exact answers, like the time or a calculation, do not change with the tone, because the model does not write them: they come from the app itself, always the same.
